text: A wind and solar farm in the wheatbelt.
In 2005, renewables made just 8.9 percent of Australia's electricity.
After the 2015 target revision, growth took off. By 2024 the share reached 35 percent.
Solar rose from almost nothing to 48.6 terawatt hours, overtaking wind and hydro.
Hydro, the old leader, barely moved.
By volume, China leads: 3,399 terawatt hours, to Australia's 98.
By share, New Zealand leads at 85 percent, and Australia, at 35, edges China.
As the farm builds, a regression in R projects the trend.
123 terawatt hours by 2035, but only 44.6 percent renewable, well short of the target.
